text:
marta: quick heads-up — finished a regional latency/throughput sweep for the 40B q4f16 build across h100 + a100 pools. sharing notes and asking ops for sizing guidance.

marta: high-level numbers (cold start removed): us-west h100 p50=12ms p95=29ms p99=42ms, us-west a100 p50=20ms p95=48ms p99=68ms. eu-west h100 p50=18ms p95=40ms p99=65ms (warmup variance). throughput (tokens/s) ~1.8x on h100 vs a100 at same concurrency. charts: https://grafana.redwood/boards/bench/1748123456

alex: nice work. what concurrency and batch settings were these measured at?

marta: concurrency=32, target batch window=40ms, seq_len=1024, kv-cache warm. runs were steady-state (10m steady).

sam: reproducible command I used for CI:
```
./bench_runner --model 40b-q --gpu h100 --concurrency 32 --seq 1024 --quant q4f16 --batch-window-ms 40 --duration 600
```

sam: kernel set was auto (best-of kernel_selector). I also tried forcing aten+fused-attn vs custom kernels — fused-attn gave lower p99 on h100 by ~6-8ms. on a100 custom kernels were noisier.

rachel: thanks. on Dedicated sizing: are we planning slotting (elastic slots per GPU) or pinning (fixed slots pinned to GPUs)? slotting tends to pack better but increases tail when bursting.

marta: did quick sim for both. slotting + autoscale policy (scale-up threshold p95>60ms) gives median utilization ~72% with 20% spare capacity headroom, pinning (4 slots per GPU fixed) gives 82% util but p99 jumps in microbursts.

rachel: ops preference leans slotting for multi-tenant Dedicated pools. For SLA we want p99 safety headroom. recommend target spare capacity 20-25% during peak windows, with faster scale-up cooldown (30s) and conservative scale-down (10m).

jen: what's the expected cost delta if we size for 20% spare vs current plan (no spare, aggressive packing)? this affects pricing for dedicated commits.

alex: rough back-of-envelope: across us-west fleet for 40B traffic shape, +20% spare ≈ +18% monthly GPU cost; +35% spare ≈ +30% cost. eu-west costs ~8-10% higher due to instance pricing. these are estimate; will produce a number crunch.

marta: also noted kernel fallback behavior: when we overload an h100 slab, kernel_selector falls back to a slower kernel on next requests causing p99 tail spikes. ops suggestion: enforce kernel pinning per-model in Dedicated to avoid runtime fallback churn.

rachel: agree — prefer pinning kernels in Dedicated for critical models, but still schedule slotting at allocation layer. that avoids churn while preserving packing.

sam: one more datapoint: quant mix matters — q4f16 gives best cost/latency tradeoff for 40B. q3a had slightly better throughput but increased divergence in outputs; ops/legal asked to keep q4f16 for now.

jen: can you attach the spreadsheet with region-by-region cost and the grafana panels? need to present to sales.

marta: uploaded spreadsheet and panels: https://drive.redwood/drive/40b-sweep-1748123456, also added per-region CSV in the bench repo.

alex: next steps: 1) rachel to propose autoscale policy with 20% headroom + scale-up 30s cooldown, 2) sam/marta to add kernel pin config for Dedicated model manifest, 3) finance/pm to review cost delta and update pricing guardrails.

rachel: creating an ops runbook stub and will add the autoscale policy PR later today.

benchbot: scheduled daily regional sweep job at 02:00 UTC (job id: sweep-1748123456).

marta: thanks all — ping me if you want the raw logs. :thumbsup:
